excluded_stale_test.reason: This command ran after a failed build without a fail-fast shell and used the prior executable; explicitly excluded from acceptance. Subsequent commands gated tests on successful build.

guarantees: Explicit retained native-End scan pin prevents directory-owner retirement before refresh preparation; default release-at-End behavior remains. All native owners retire on workers.

Incremental preparation is bounded to 256 steps per advance and cooperative injected-clock slices; names capped at 1 MiB and pane limits checked before retained copies. No partial prepared payload is published.

Both parent handles are alive during scoped ID comparison. Unknown/different parents decline child I/O; only live immutable HeldChild successors can preserve row IDs, focus and marks at final publication.
Named binding issues distinguish replacements, failed/unqualified continuity and unlisted observations. Current metadata/hidden policy is refreshed, including hidden-mark review semantics.

Cancellation checks inside held-child native query sequences close private children. Paused work resumes; abandonment/fatal errors release staging; generation cancellation and supersession reject late payloads.

Exception poisoning uses empty diagnostic text and in-place nonthrowing payload movement with compile-time construction/destruction checks; bad_alloc leaves the old published pane and native owners intact.
limitations: Only already-held entries receive qualified refresh continuity. Initial selection pinning, UI ownership/scheduling and large-view indexes remain required.
Native identity observations rely on adapter/native ID contracts and are not pathname attestation, a namespace/content snapshot or operation authority.
No hard deadline across blocking native calls, allocator/encoder work, or global process-memory quota; old pane, raw payload, staging and prepared projection can coexist.
Issue details describe the latest published refresh, not a persistent selection-event journal; invalidation counts persist until acknowledged.
No complete collision/capability planning, frozen inventories, user loss consent, mutation engine or GUI added; WP-01 remains open.
validation_notes: Final common 99-file manifest verified on all hosts. All 37 Files suites passed: 264 Mac /262 Linux /268 Windows cases, including the new allocation-failure test marker in every LastTest log.

Initial 18-step Mac build took 20.020 seconds including CMake regeneration and affected/new fixtures. Review tests and scan-pin getter naming produced later 2-step/11-step increments. Final successful Mac build used four remaining compile/link steps (1.549 seconds); unchanged test objects from the failed attempt were valid for the final source, while the repaired implementation and both executables rebuilt.

Two compile-time noexcept assumptions about optional wrapper operations were rejected; no flags were weakened. Payload move/destruction traits plus the specified optional::emplace exception guarantee provide the final nonthrowing poison path. The first accidentally executed stale CTest result is recorded but explicitly excluded. Fail-fast validation then succeeded.
Final Linux/Windows incremental builds took 3.665/9.358 seconds and performed six intended steps. Source hashes, logs and the newly linked bad_alloc case establish freshness, not elapsed time alone.

Direct sanitizers use fresh directories and all listed units with strict warnings/halt-on-error: Mac 50.750 seconds build/.499 test, Windows 88.656/1.266. Pre-oom same-scope Mac build was 51.641 seconds with 86 cases; final adds the bad_alloc case. Previous narrower 28-unit builds were 44.833/64.181, not identical-scope baselines. Exact lists, flags, source hashes and emitted Windows units checked.

Linux 35-unit ASan+UBSan build took 121.538 seconds, test .373, on a private casefold-enabled ext4 image. It includes the full affected fixture set plus required native casefold qualification. Previous 29-unit different-fixture build was 87.946 seconds; this records the broader baseline.

Linux image unmounted, loop audit empty, diagnostic/image workspace removed; final remote audit finds it absent, fixtures empty and no owned tests live. Mac/Windows diagnostics hashed and zero owners recorded before disposal. Current normal builds retained; Windows development writes/temp stayed on V:.
